title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for diabetes and numbness in feet.

HPI
The patient is a 62-year-old individual presenting for a routine follow-up of type 2 diabetes mellitus. The patient reports ongoing symptoms of polyneuropathy, characterized by a persistent tingling and "pins and needles" sensation in both feet. These symptoms have been stable over the last three months. The patient reports adherence to their current medication regimen and denies any recent falls or acute injuries to the lower extremities.

Medication List
- Insulin
- Metformin
- Glipizide

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Physical examination of the lower extremities reveals diminished sensation to light touch and vibration in the toes. Muscle strength is 5/5 in both legs. No visible ulcers or skin breakdown noted on the feet.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus
2. Polyneuropathy

Plan
Continue current regimen of insulin and oral hypoglycemic agents. The patient will continue to monitor blood glucose levels daily. We will schedule a follow-up in three months to monitor the progression of the peripheral neuropathy and evaluate the need for any dosage adjustments.
explanations: Polyneuropathy is listed under 'with' for diabetes: the combination code E11.42 captures both.
When both insulin and oral hypoglycemics are used, assign both Z79.4 and Z79.84.

distractors.why: Coding the two separately misses the presumed link.
Both Z codes are assigned when both drug types are used.
